week.title: Gregor's New Life

opening_illustration.alt_text: Grete enters Gregor's dim bedroom with a tray of food. Gregor is partly hidden under the sofa. Grete looks careful and nervous.

part_illustrations.alt_text: Grete brings milk and bread into Gregor's dim bedroom while he hides under the sofa.
The milk remains untouched while Grete offers Gregor several different foods.
Gregor hides under the sofa and a cloth while Grete carefully cleans the room.
Gregor listens from his dark room while his family discusses money in the brighter room.
Gregor climbs the bedroom wall as Grete notices that the furniture limits his movement.
Gregor looks at his desk, chair and picture and worries about losing the last signs of his human life.

before_you_read: Who takes care of you when you are sick?
Is helping your family important to you?
How do you feel when you cannot do something you normally do?
story: Gregor stays inside his bedroom.
The door is closed.
His body hurts after what happened with his father.
The apartment is quiet.
Gregor is hungry.
After some time, the bedroom door opens slowly.
Grete enters.
She carries a bowl of milk and some bread.
Before his transformation, Gregor likes milk very much. Grete remembers this.
She puts the food near him and quickly leaves the room.
Gregor waits. Then he moves toward the bowl. He tries the milk.
But something is different. He does not like it now.
Later, Grete returns. She understands that Gregor does not want the milk.
The next time, she brings many different foods. There are old vegetables. There is cheese. There is bread. There are sauces and other things from the kitchen.
Gregor tries them. Now he likes some foods that he did not like before. His body is different. His taste is different too.
Grete begins to understand his new habits. Every day, she brings food. Every day, she cleans part of his room.
But she is still afraid of him.
Gregor understands this. When Grete enters, he often hides under the sofa. He does not want to frighten her.
Sometimes, only part of his body fits under it. Gregor puts a cloth over himself. Now Grete can enter the room without looking directly at him.
Gregor watches his sister quietly. He knows she is trying to help him. He is grateful. But he is also sad.
He cannot speak to her. He cannot say, “Thank you.” He cannot ask, “How are you?” He cannot tell her that he is still her brother.
Gregor spends many hours alone. He listens to his family through the door.
In the evening, his father and mother talk about money. Gregor listens carefully.
Before his transformation, Gregor works every day. He pays for many things in the family. He believes his family has almost no money.
But now he hears something new. His father still has some money from the past. It is not a lot. The family can live with it for some time. But not forever.
Soon, everyone needs to work.
Gregor feels something strange. He is happy because his family has some money. But he also feels guilty.
His father must work again. His mother needs to help. Grete is young, but she will need more responsibilities too.
Gregor remembers his old life. He gets up early. He takes trains. He travels. He works for many hours. He comes home tired.
He does not like that life. But the money helps his family.
Now Gregor cannot help them. He stays in his room. The family works outside it.
Days pass. Gregor slowly learns how to use his new body. He moves across the floor. Then he begins to climb the walls.
Sometimes, he climbs high and stays there. Movement makes him feel better.
Grete notices this. She looks at the furniture in the bedroom. There is a bed. There is a desk. There are chairs and other things from Gregor's old life.
Grete has an idea. Maybe Gregor needs more space. Maybe the furniture is now a problem for him. She thinks about removing it.
Gregor listens. At first, the idea sounds practical. More space means he can move more easily.
But then Gregor looks around the room. He looks at his desk. His chair. His picture.
These things belong to his human life.
Gregor asks himself a question:
If the room changes completely...
what is left of his old life?

visual_reflection.title: Gregor Listens to His Family
visual_reflection.alt_text: Gregor stays close to the bedroom door in the darker room while his family talks together in the brighter room beyond. He is physically near them but separated.
questions: What does the light and distance show about Gregor's situation?

items: He ______ to his family through the door.

reading_comprehension.question: What food does Grete bring first?
Why does Grete bring different foods?
reading_comprehension.suggested_answer: Because she wants to discover what Gregor likes now.

reading_comprehension.question: Why does Gregor hide under the sofa?
reading_comprehension.suggested_answer: Because he does not want to frighten Grete.

reading_comprehension.question: How does Grete help Gregor every day?
reading_comprehension.suggested_answer: She brings food and cleans part of his room.

reading_comprehension.question: What does Gregor hear his family talking about?
reading_comprehension.suggested_answer: Money and the family's financial situation.

reading_comprehension.question: Does the family have some money?
reading_comprehension.suggested_answer: Yes. Gregor's father has some money from the past.

reading_comprehension.question: Why does Gregor feel guilty?
reading_comprehension.suggested_answer: Because he cannot work or support his family now.

reading_comprehension.question: What new thing can Gregor do with his body?
Why does Gregor feel worried about removing the furniture?
reading_comprehension.suggested_answer: Because the furniture connects him to his old human life.

true_false.statement: Grete brings different foods to Gregor.
Gregor hides because he wants to scare Grete.
Gregor listens to his family through the door.
Gregor is happy because he cannot work.
Gregor begins to climb the walls.

grammar_focus.title: Simple Present — Daily Routine
grammar_focus.rule: With he, she and it, we usually add -s to the verb. Use does not / doesn't + base verb for negatives.

items: Grete bring / brings food to Gregor.
Gregor stay / stays in his bedroom.
Gregor listen / listens to his family.

writing_mission.title: A Day in Gregor's New Life
writing_mission.instruction: Write about a day in Gregor's new life.

story_image_activity.title: Gregor Listens to His Family
questions: Can Gregor participate in the conversation?
How does this make him feel?

kafkas_question.prompt: Is Gregor less important because he cannot work?

deeper_question.prompt: Who is Gregor protecting: himself or Grete?

prediction.question: What do you think Gregor wants?

learning_outcomes: Describe how Grete cares for Gregor.
Think about the relationship between work and personal value.

next_week.teaser: Grete wants to help Gregor. She wants to give him more space. But removing the furniture may mean removing something else too: Gregor's old life.
